title: Martin, Benedict, Nicholas hymns: foster prelates, clothe with justice, grant perennial kingdoms and life’s aid
source_text: LV. Ad Sanctum quoque Martinum cani solet hic hymnus, Martine par Apostolis, Festum colentes tu fove, Qui vivere Discipulos Vis aut mori, nostros respice. Fac ut quod olim gesseras, Nunc praesules clarifica, Auge decus Ecclesiae, Fraudes elude Satanae. Qui ter Chaos eviceras, Mersos reatu suscita: Diviseras ut Chlamydem, Nos indue justitia. Denique Sancto Benedicto dicitur in hymno de ejus translatione, Angustum per iter scandere largiens, Dona regna perennia. Et in hymno de Sancto Nicolao qui incipit, Exultet aula caelica, haec dirigitur ad ipsum precatio, O Venerande Pontifex, Pius nec tardus opifex, Cunctis qui corde credulo, Te quaerunt in periculo, Aufer mortis dispendia, Confer vitae subsidia; Ut post carnis exilia, Tecum simus in gloria.
pass_a_gloss: To Saint Martin also this hymn is accustomed to be sung: Martin equal to the Apostles, Foster those celebrating thy feast, Who willest disciples to live or die, look on ours. Cause that what thou once didst, Now glorify prelates, Increase the honor of the Church, Elude the frauds of Satan. Thou who thrice hadst overcome Chaos, Raise those sunk in guilt: As thou hadst divided the cloak, Clothe us with justice. Finally to Saint Benedict it is said in the hymn on his translation, Granting to climb the narrow way, Give perennial kingdoms. And in the hymn on Saint Nicholas which begins Exultet aula caelica, this prayer is directed to him: O Venerable Pontiff, Pious nor slow craftsman, To all who with believing heart Seek thee in danger, Take away the losses of death, Confer the supports of life; That after the exiles of the flesh We may be with thee in glory.
pass_b_english: Martin’s hymn asks him to foster the feast, clarify prelates, and clothe us as he once shared his cloak.
Benedict: help climb the narrow way to perennial kingdoms; Nicholas: strip death’s losses and grant life’s aid unto glory.

choices.why: Incipit of the public Martin hymn cited.
